content.weeklyOverview: Tiny Artist Studio introduces babies to their first creative experiences through adorable caregiver-assisted handprint and footprint keepsakes, mess-free color exploration, safe sensory art, movement, texture, and visual discovery. Babies are never expected to complete a craft. Instead, caregivers build meaningful art experiences around natural infant behaviors such as looking, kicking, reaching, opening and closing hands, patting, pressing, and responding to new sensations. The week combines cute family-worthy keepsakes with genuine developmental experiences involving body awareness, sensory processing, visual attention, cause and effect, communication, and caregiver bonding.
content.title: Tiny Artist Studio

objectives: Explore color through safe visual and sensory experiences.
Build awareness of hands, fingers, feet, and toes.
Practice natural reaching, kicking, patting, and pressing movements.
Respond to caregiver narration and facial expressions.
Build caregiver-infant connection through one-to-one interaction.
Show preferences through gaze, movement, expression, or vocalization.
Participate in early creative experiences without pressure for a finished product.

activities.title: My First Handprint
activities.description: Baby feels a very small amount of washable paint on the palm while a caregiver gently creates one natural handprint.
activities.purpose: Baby feels a very small amount of washable paint on the palm while a caregiver gently creates one natural handprint.
activities.materialsText:
Washable non-toxic paint
Heavy cardstock
Warm washcloth
Protective surface
activities.learningObjective: Introduce gentle tactile exploration while helping baby notice their hand and fingers.

teacherPrompts.label: Tip
teacherPrompts.text: One imperfect print is enough.

activities.setup: Hold or position baby securely with continuous adult support.
activities.steps:
Talk about baby's hand.
Allow baby to see the caregiver's face and hear calm narration.
Apply a thin amount of paint to the palm.
Pause and observe baby's reaction.
If baby remains comfortable, gently bring the hand to cardstock.
Allow the natural hand position to create the print.
Lift the hand without forcing fingers open.
Clean immediately.
activities.preparation: Have cardstock, paint, and a warm washcloth completely ready before beginning.
cleanupTips: Wash baby's hand thoroughly and sanitize the area.
observationIdeas: Observe tactile response, natural hand opening, visual attention, and caregiver interaction.
activities.safetyNotes: Never force fingers open. Stop for distress, mouthing, or skin irritation.

activities.title: My First Handprint
activities.description: Baby feels a very small amount of washable paint on the palm while a caregiver gently creates one natural handprint.
activities.purpose: Baby feels a very small amount of washable paint on the palm while a caregiver gently creates one natural handprint.
activities.materialsText:
Washable non-toxic paint
Heavy cardstock
Warm washcloth
Protective surface
activities.learningObjective: Introduce gentle tactile exploration while helping baby notice their hand and fingers.

teacherPrompts.label: Tip
teacherPrompts.text: One imperfect print is enough.

activities.setup: Hold or position baby securely with continuous adult support.
activities.steps:
Talk about baby's hand.
Allow baby to see the caregiver's face and hear calm narration.
Apply a thin amount of paint to the palm.
Pause and observe baby's reaction.
If baby remains comfortable, gently bring the hand to cardstock.
Allow the natural hand position to create the print.
Lift the hand without forcing fingers open.
Clean immediately.
activities.preparation: Have cardstock, paint, and a warm washcloth completely ready before beginning.
cleanupTips: Wash baby's hand thoroughly and sanitize the area.
observationIdeas: Observe tactile response, natural hand opening, visual attention, and caregiver interaction.
activities.safetyNotes: Never force fingers open. Stop for distress, mouthing, or skin irritation.
